name: Scaling Continues
tagline: Frontier models and giant compute stay central; capital intensity is the moat.
confidenceNote: The most historically predictive causal model in the dataset (Bitter Lesson, scaling laws, Jevons, infra supercycle) points here, and 2024–26 leading indicators (capex, lab revenue, reasoning-compute demand) are all observed. It breaks if revenue fails to close the capex gap or if a power/financing shock hits.

energy.state: GW-scale campuses and on-site generation are the unit of competition; power is the binding constraint.

semis.state: Nvidia plus hyperscaler ASICs; HBM and advanced packaging stay scarce.

cloud.state: A few hyperscalers and neoclouds run multi-GW fleets under long-term contracts.

data.state: RL environments, synthetic and agentic interaction data become the main training input.

architecture.state: Transformer-based backbones with MoE and long-context improvements; incremental change.

training.state: RL and post-training compute rival pretraining; continual scaling of both.

inference.state: Reasoning and agents multiply tokens per task; unit prices fall, total spend rises.

models.state: 3–5 frontier labs hold a capability lead of 6–12 months over open models.

platforms.state: Lab-owned agent platforms and hyperscaler AI platforms dominate tooling.

agents.state: Agents automate software engineering and parts of knowledge work, scaling with model capability.

apps.state: Apps built on frontier APIs; labs move up-stack into the most valuable categories.

distribution.state: Assistants become the default interface; incumbents with devices and suites hold share.

economics.state: Value concentrates in chips, power and frontier labs; scale is the moat.

society.state: National-security framing of frontier AI; compute governance and export controls tighten.

advantage: Access to capital and long-term compute contracts
capitalIntensity: Extreme and rising: annual AI capex well above the ~$700B of 2026, financed increasingly by debt and sovereign capital.
enterprise: Enterprises buy capability from a few labs/clouds; spend shifts to agentic services priced per task; vendor concentration risk rises.
assumptions: Revenue grows fast enough to finance capex
No efficiency shock collapses compute demand
Power can be built fast enough

indicators.text: Big-four capex guidance rising year over year (≈$700B+ in 2026)
Lab revenue run-rates compounding >2x per year (~$65–70B by Sep 2026)
Frontier model releases keep widening the gap over open weights
Capex financing shifts to bonds/private credit without spread blowouts

invalidators: A sustained capex cut by two or more hyperscalers
Frontier releases stall for 12+ months despite more compute
An open model matches the frontier at a fraction of the cost and holds
Credit event at a major AI infrastructure borrower

supporters.why: AI factories and reasoning compute imply a multi-trillion build-out.
OOM counting: GW → 10 GW → 100 GW clusters.
Scaling laws plus RL keep delivering.
Compute is the input; 30 GW committed.
The Bitter Lesson: general methods + compute win.

challengers.why: Age of scaling is over; research is the bottleneck.
Revenue gap makes the capex trajectory fragile.
Scaling yields diminishing returns on reliability.

name: Intelligence Commoditizes
tagline: Open weights and efficiency compress model margins; value migrates to data, workflow and distribution.
confidenceNote: Strongly supported on price (fixed-capability cost falling ~10x/yr; open weights months behind) but contradicted, so far, on margins: frontier labs' revenue grew rather than shrinking. It becomes dominant if the frontier gap stops mattering for most workloads.

energy.state: Power still matters but demand growth slows as efficiency outpaces usage.

semis.state: Inference-optimized and edge chips gain; GPU pricing power erodes.

cloud.state: Overbuilt capacity; GPU-hour prices fall; neoclouds consolidate.

data.state: Proprietary enterprise data and feedback loops become the differentiator.

architecture.state: Efficiency innovations (MoE, distillation, new attention) diffuse within weeks.

training.state: Distillation and fine-tuning of open bases dominate; few frontier pretraining runs.

inference.state: Cost per task collapses; small models run on device and on-prem.

models.state: Open-weight models within weeks of the frontier for most tasks; models interchangeable.

platforms.state: Routing, evaluation, security and governance platforms capture value.

agents.state: Agent frameworks are open; value sits in workflow integration.

apps.state: Vertical apps with proprietary data and distribution win.

distribution.state: OS, browser, suite and marketplace owners control access to users.

economics.state: Value migrates from model layer to data, distribution and workflow ownership.

society.state: Proliferation of capable open models complicates governance; national open-model champions.

capitalIntensity: Falls after 2027 as overbuilt capacity is absorbed; write-downs on GPU fleets.
enterprise: Buying shifts from models to platforms, workflows and outcomes; multi-model routing becomes standard; on-prem/open models for sensitive data.
assumptions: Capability plateaus relative to task needs

indicators.text: Open-weight lag vs frontier at 3–4 months (Epoch)
Frontier labs' gross margins and price per token at the top tier falling
Enterprise share of spend going to open/self-hosted models rising
GPU rental prices and utilization falling

invalidators: Frontier labs sustain premium pricing and >50% revenue growth
A capability jump (e.g. reliable agents) only available from closed models

supporters.why: Closed moats are temporary; price near cost.
Selling intelligence may be like selling rice.
Efficient labs approach frontier with a fraction of compute.
Jevons: AI becomes a commodity we can't get enough of.

challengers.why: Frontier capability gaps persist and command premium.
Frontier AI should not be open-sourced.

name: Agentic & Architectural Transformation
tagline: Reliable agents, memory, continual learning or world models reshape the stack around outcomes.
confidenceNote: Coding agents already show the pattern (2025–26), and METR task horizons doubling ~every 7 months is the strongest leading indicator. But general-purpose reliability, continual learning and world models were still research problems at the cutoff, and the most specific near-term agent forecasts were early.

energy.state: Demand driven by always-on agents; inference dominates power use.

semis.state: Inference and memory-bandwidth-optimized silicon; on-device agents.

cloud.state: Agent runtimes, sandboxes and long-running compute become cloud products.

data.state: Experience data from agents' own interactions; persistent memory as an asset.

architecture.state: Memory, continual learning and world-model components join or replace pure next-token models.

training.state: Online/experiential learning (Era of Experience) supplements batch pretraining.

inference.state: Long-horizon test-time computation; cost per outcome replaces cost per token.

models.state: Models become components inside agent systems; capability measured by task completion.

platforms.state: Agent identity, permissions, audit and evaluation become critical infrastructure.

agents.state: Agents run multi-day tasks reliably in many functions; humans supervise portfolios of agents.

apps.state: Apps restructure as agents sold on outcomes; seat-based SaaS erodes.

distribution.state: Whoever owns the agent the user delegates to owns the customer.

economics.state: Pricing shifts to outcomes and labor budgets; value accrues to agent owners and trusted platforms.

society.state: Labor-market restructuring, especially entry-level knowledge work; liability and agent identity regulation.

bottlenecks: Security and permissioning of autonomous actions
advantage: Memory and context about users and firms
controlPoints: Systems of record agents act on

winners.who: Agent platforms with trust and memory
Security, identity and audit for agents

capitalIntensity: High but shifting from training to inference and agent runtimes; new spend on security and evaluation.
enterprise: Buyers purchase outcomes (resolved tickets, shipped code) rather than models or seats; ROI becomes measurable per task.

indicators.text: METR 50% task horizon doubling ~every 7 months (≈5h by 2026)
Coding agents writing most code at leading firms
Outcome-based pricing spreading beyond software engineering
Published continual-learning or world-model systems deployed at scale

invalidators: Task-horizon growth stalls for a year
Major agent security incidents trigger restrictions
Enterprise agent deployments fail to show P&L impact through 2028

supporters.why: Coding agents crossed a coherence threshold; LLM OS.
Era of Experience: agents learn from their own streams.
World models and memory are the next paradigm.
World models, planning and continual learning are missing pieces.

challengers.why: It's a decade of agents, not a year.
